title: 2026 Michigan gubernatorial election
description: Michigan’s 2026 gubernatorial election will choose the state’s next governor after term-limited Democrat Gretchen Whitmer leaves office. The race is open and has drawn attention because it could shift partisan control of a major battleground state that has voted closely in recent presidential elections. Early coverage and polling have centered on a likely Democratic nominee in Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson, Republicans John James and Mike Cox, and independent former Detroit Mayor Mike Duggan. The contest is being shaped by contrasts over experience, party alignment, and whether an independent candidacy can change the general-election math.

reviews.summary: This is a well-sourced, comprehensive profile of the 2026 Michigan gubernatorial race. All four major candidates (Benson, Cox, Duggan, James) are covered with detailed issue positions backed by citations to official campaign sites, credible news outlets (Bridge Michigan, Detroit Free Press, MLive, Michigan Public Radio), and government records. The polling data spans recent months (November 2025–February 2026) with appropriate sample sizes and sourcing. Candidate backgrounds are documented consistently with cited sources. Language is neutral and nonpartisan throughout. Missing positions on some issues (e.g., immigration for Benson and Duggan) are appropriately marked as "no public position found" after good-faith search attempts. Congressional voting records for John James are properly cited to House Clerk and Vote Smart records. The profile demonstrates balanced coverage of a competitive open-seat race with one Democratic, two Republican, and one independent major candidate.

reviews.summary: Strong overall profile with comprehensive sourcing from campaign sites, news outlets, and official records across all candidates and issues. Polling data is well-cited and current; backgrounds and issues stances are detailed and neutral. Minor issues include one incorrect image URL for John James and a few donor/top_donor mismatches using outdated cycles, plus occasional future-dated sources that align with profile timestamps but warrant spot-check.

polling_note: Recent polling in February 2026 shows a competitive race, with Benson leading in some matchups and the field remaining close in others. Polls cited here are from the last 90 days and include both a campaign-commissioned Impact Research survey and a Detroit Regional Chamber/Glengariff Group poll.

validation_grade.summary: Validated by 2/3 reviewers with an average score of 89/100.
